hook.h2: He did not accept "I'm too young" as an answer
hook.text: I said, "Ah, Sovereign Father! I don't know how to speak, for I'm only a boy." But our Father said to me, 'Don't say, "I'm only a youth," for you'll go wherever I send you and speak whatever I command.'
father: But our Father said to me, 'Don't say,
for you'll go wherever I send you and speak whatever I command.'
hook.note: Jeremiah's first move was to tell our Father he was too young for this, and our Father did not agree with him. That is the exchange this edition is built around. At seventeen you are old enough to be given something real, and the one objection everyone raises at that age is the one He answers here — in BLUE, in His own voice, on the page.

short350: You have wanted a Father your whole life. Not a doctrine about Him. Not a distant power. A Father — His voice, His heart turned toward you.
Father's Heart Bible is the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's in RED. The Spirit's in PURPLE.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking. The color marks ownership, not quotation: His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, words He never spoke are never colored, and narration stays black.

Scripture names the age: Joseph was seventeen. The dreams came before he understood them, the pit came before the palace, and through all of it our Father was with him. He is with you at the same age.

Seventeen is the year a lot of people first read the Bible because they want to, rather than because somebody handed it to them. It is the year the questions get real and the answers stop being borrowed. This edition was made for that year — a complete Bible, given whole, with nothing simplified and nothing held back.
That is what this Bible was made to do. Not to tell you about a Father who speaks, but to show you where He already has.

He is not distant. He is not disappointed. He is your Heavenly Father, and He delights in you as His beloved child. If father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you: the Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood, but the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

An introduction opens each book, a Father's note closes each with a short prayer, and 1,354 notes serve the reader, not the scholar. A presentation page carries their name. Six by nine, hardcover, full color throughout.
A fresh translation from the original Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek — complete, 66 books and 31,085 verses. A gift, a keepsake, an heirloom.
Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.

long.h: Seventeen Is The Age A Lot Of People First Read The Bible For Themselves
body: Your Father has been waiting to talk to you.

Scripture gives Joseph's age outright. He was seventeen when the dreams started, and long before any of it made sense, our Father was already with him. "Joseph, a young man of seventeen, tended the flock with his brothers." — Genesis 37:2

Your Father was with him at seventeen, in the pit, and in the palace. He is with you now, at the start of it. It is a devotional Bible for daily Bible reading and intimacy with God, so you hear Him for yourself.

This is not a beginner's Bible or a shortened one. It is the whole thing — 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,085 verses — given to a seventeen-year-old on the assumption they can handle it, because they can.

long.h: A Three Color Bible: Red Letter, Blue Letter, Purple Letter

Which means you can open it anywhere and see the difference between what He said and what people said about Him — including the people in the story who got Him wrong.

God is our Father. Not a role He plays. Father is who He is, and Father is His name, the name Jesus came to reveal: "I revealed your name to those you gave me from the world" (John 17:6). This translation lets the Hebrew and Greek speak the distinction they always made: God as Father, Abba Father, your Heavenly Father — and you, His beloved child.

If the word father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you. The Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood. He is the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.
You are His beloved child, and He delights in you.

faq.q: Why an edition just for seventeen?
faq.a: Because seventeen is the age a lot of people first read the Bible because they decided to. It is also the one age Scripture puts a number on for the same reason — Joseph was seventeen when the dreams started, years before any of it made sense. The opening pages are written to that, and to the fact that a seventeen-year-old is being given the complete Bible rather than a version of it.

faq.q: How is this different from the Teen Bible?
faq.a: The translation, the 876 pages and every word from Genesis 1:1 to Revelation 22:21 are identical. What differs is the cover and the opening pages: the Teen Bible speaks to ages 13–19 broadly, and the Seventeen Bible speaks to one year — the year someone is stepping out of the house they grew up in. Buy whichever one will be recognized as theirs.

faq.q: Is it a good 17th birthday or graduation gift?
faq.a: It is made for it. A complete hardcover Bible with a dust jacket and a presentation page for their name, in a cover built for a seventeen-year-old rather than a children's Bible or a generic pew edition. It will not be outgrown — it reads at the same level as every other edition, so it carries them into adulthood.

faq.q: Will a seventeen-year-old actually read it?
faq.a: It is a fresh translation in clear contemporary English, and it reads about 135,000 words shorter than the King James because modern English says the same thing in fewer words. Every book opens with an introduction telling them what it is, and the color means they can find our Father speaking on any page without hunting for it.

For a hundred and twenty-five years red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and until now those words were printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. In Divine Voice Color you see who is speaking: our Father's words in BLUE, the Son's in RED, the Spirit's in PURPLE. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking. The color is a mark of ownership, not of quotation — His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored.

faq.q: Can they read it online too?
faq.a: Yes, free, in twenty-five languages, at fathersheartbible.com/read — with English and Telugu also free to listen to. The print edition is the one that carries their name on the presentation page.
